content.text: What This Actually Is and Why It Matters: Github pages

GitHub Pages is a free static site hosting service. It serves HTML, CSS, and JavaScript directly from a GitHub repository. For digital creators, this means a storefront without hosting costs. Combined with Google Apps Script for backend logic and NOWPayments for crypto transactions, it becomes a fully functional store. The architecture is sovereign: no platform dependence, no recurring fees. You retain 99.5% of revenue versus Gumroad’s 90%. At 100 sales of a $97 product monthly, this retains $921 more. The system is pressure-tested in regions like Zimbabwe, where currency collapse and payment rejections are realities, not hypotheticals.
How the Architecture Works Under the Hood

The frontend is hosted on GitHub Pages. A simple HTML/CSS template displays products. When a buyer selects a product, a Google Apps Script backend processes the order. NOWPayments handles the crypto transaction, verifying payment on-chain. Once confirmed, the script triggers automatic file delivery via Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. Order data is logged in Google Sheets for tracking. The system is stateless: no database required. Payment verification is instantaneous via NOWPayments webhooks. The entire stack is serverless, with no ongoing costs. You own the code, the data, and the deployment—no third-party access after setup.
Who This Is Built For and Why

This architecture is for digital creators in regions where conventional payment processors are restricted or unreliable. It’s designed for selling ebooks, courses, templates, fonts, presets, beats, plugins, and software. If you’re in Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Pakistan, or Venezuela, this stack bypasses Stripe and PayPal entirely. It’s also for creators who refuse platform lock-in. Gumroad and Payhip charge fees and control your customer relationship. This system puts you in full control. Deploy once, own forever. No subscriptions. No platform risk. Infrastructure sovereignty is the core principle.
GitHub Pages is free, globally accessible, and serves your storefront directly from a repository.
The Components That Make It Work Together

GitHub Pages hosts the storefront. Google Apps Script handles backend logic, including order processing and file delivery. NOWPayments integrates crypto payments with 0.5% fees and no KYC. Google Sheets stores order data. Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 delivers files securely. The stack is modular: swap components as needed. For example, replace Google Apps Script with Cloudflare Workers for edge computing. Use Supabase instead of Google Sheets for structured data. Each component is chosen for cost-efficiency and sovereignty. The system is open-source, with no vendor lock-in. You own the deployment and can modify it at will.
How to Use This Knowledge to Deploy Today

Start by forking a GitHub Pages template for digital product stores. Integrate NOWPayments for crypto checkout. Write a Google Apps Script to handle order processing and file delivery. Test the flow end-to-end. Deploy to GitHub Pages. Load your first three products. Own your store. Own your revenue. Own your infrastructure.

Frequently Asked Questions
Can I use this stack if I’m not a developer?
Yes. The Sovereign Starter Stack ($97) deploys the architecture for you in 48 hours, including three products and 30-day support. No coding required. Own the deployed system fully.
What cryptocurrencies does NOWPayments support?
NOWPayments supports 300+ cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, USDT, and stablecoins on BSC, Solana, and TRON networks for low fees under $0.10 per transaction.
How do I handle refunds or chargebacks?
Crypto transactions are irreversible. Clearly communicate this in your store’s terms. For disputes, use order data from Google Sheets to resolve issues directly with the buyer.
Can I scale this beyond three products?
Yes. The Edge Commerce Stack ($197) includes SPF/DKIM/DMARC configuration and supports five products. For larger catalogs, use the Sovereign Blueprint ($47) for scaling guidance.
What happens if GitHub Pages or Google services go down?
GitHub Pages has 99.9% uptime. Google services are enterprise-grade. For redundancy, deploy to Cloudflare Pages and use Supabase for data storage. The stack is modular and adaptable.
